note: Definitions for the passage annotations (schema in the docstring of input/check_kl.py). v2 (plan-fix group 1): table_data is no longer a scope but the flag is_table (g1-2); one home per named company, canonical names in input/companies.json (g1-9, g1-15); new themes for investing principles, preferreds, arbitrage, pensions and shareholder programs (g1-6); tie-break sentences for overlapping keys; scope rules and anchor examples (g1-20). Built from corpus reading and counts only, without test-set access.
annotation_rules: scope is financial whenever the passage has any financial content; if it also has personal content, set has_personal.
Tag only what the passage is really ABOUT, not passing mentions.
periods are the years the passage discusses, which is not always the letter year.
stance only where Buffett clearly judges a sector, company or theme; quote his words verbatim; the target is a sector key, a theme key or a canonical company name.
summary covers the financial point only ('' when scope is not financial); for a table, name what the table lists.

scope.financial: Any financial content: markets, economy, crises, sectors, companies' economics, Berkshire results, investing, capital allocation, accounting, insurance, management/governance as it affects owners. Use this when a passage mixes financial and personal content (set has_personal true). Tables of numbers are financial too (set is_table true).
scope.personal_anecdote: Biographies, family, ages, health, diet, jokes, sports, personal stories, tributes with no financial content.
scope.meeting_logistics: Annual meeting arrangements, travel, hotels, shopping discounts and meeting-weekend sales, exhibitor lists, ball games, Q&A procedure, report-ordering instructions.
scope.boilerplate_other: Salutations, signatures, page references, table footnotes, legal or proxy boilerplate, anything else without financial content.

flags.has_personal: true when the passage also contains personal content (biography, family, ages, jokes, tributes); mostly used with scope financial.
flags.is_table: true when the passage is mostly a table of numbers (holdings, performance, segment earnings, float) with little prose. A table is scope financial and carries sectors, companies and periods like any financial passage (themes optional). Its summary names what the table lists, e.g. 'Table: yearend 1990 common-stock holdings with shares, cost and market value'.

scope_rules: Shareholder programs with amounts (designated contributions, dividend or repurchase policy votes, the owner's manual) are financial, theme shareholder_programs.

Annual-meeting passages are meeting_logistics unless they report business results of Berkshire or a subsidiary for the year; meeting-weekend shopping discounts and the sales made at the meeting stay meeting_logistics.
Manager tributes are financial with has_personal true when they give results (sales, earnings, float, growth); a tribute without financial content is personal_anecdote.
A salutation or signature line inside a passage that also reports results does not change the scope: the passage is financial.
A passage that is mostly a table of numbers is financial with is_table true; a table's footnotes alone are boilerplate_other.

examples.why: salutation plus the year's net-worth and book-value result
Blumkin family tribute that gives NFM's sales results
praise of Ajit Jain ('worry about his [health]') within a discussion of float cost and retroactive reinsurance
shareholder-designated contributions with amounts and the plebiscite on dividend policy: theme shareholder_programs
yearend 1990 holdings table (shares, cost, market value)
segment earnings table, pre-tax and after-tax, 1984 vs 1983
story of the grandfather's book on grocery stores and fishing
the Blumkin family's emigration story, no financial point
tribute to Charlie Munger as Berkshire's architect, no results
annual meeting date, venue and schedule
restaurant reservations and the journalists running the Q&A
credentials, travel help and 'Berkshire Weekend' pricing at NFM with the weekend's sales: meeting-weekend sales stay logistics
how to order earlier letters, address, signature and the appendix title

sectors.insurance: property-casualty, auto, reinsurance, life/annuity, GEICO, General Re, NICO, BHRG, the insurance industry
sectors.banking: banks, thrifts, savings and loans, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Wesco Financial and its Mutual Savings, the banking industry
sectors.financial_services_other: consumer finance, credit cards (American Express), investment banks (Salomon, Goldman Sachs), asset managers, rating agencies (Moody's), commercial finance (FINOVA, Berkadia)
sectors.utilities_energy: electric and gas utilities, pipelines, renewables, MidAmerican / Berkshire Hathaway Energy, public-power issuers (WPPSS)
sectors.oil_gas: oil and gas producers and refiners, oil prices, OPEC (Occidental, ConocoPhillips, PetroChina, Chevron, Exxon Mobil, Texaco)
sectors.airlines_aviation: airlines (USAir), aircraft, NetJets / Executive Jet, FlightSafety
sectors.newspapers_publishing: newspapers and publishing (Buffalo News, Washington Post, BH Media, World Book)
sectors.tv_broadcasting_media: television, broadcasting, media franchises, advertising (Capital Cities/ABC, Disney, Interpublic)
sectors.retail: retailers in general, department stores, Nebraska Furniture Mart, RC Willey, Borsheim's, Helzberg, Tesco, Costco, Walmart
sectors.consumer_brands: branded consumer goods: Coca-Cola, See's Candies, Gillette, Kraft Heinz, Dairy Queen, Fruit of the Loom, Duracell
sectors.manufacturing_industrial: manufacturing and industrial companies: Precision Castparts, Lubrizol, Marmon, IMC/Iscar, Scott Fetzer (except Kirby), CTB, Forest River, chemicals, metal fabrication
sectors.housing_construction: home building, manufactured housing and its lending (Clayton; a Clayton lending passage also gets theme debt_leverage), building products (Shaw carpet, Johns Manville, Benjamin Moore, MiTek, Acme Brick), residential construction, real-estate brokerage (HomeServices)
sectors.textiles_apparel_shoes: Berkshire's textile mills, shoes (Dexter, H.H. Brown), apparel
sectors.technology: technology and telecom companies and the tech sector (Apple, IBM, Verizon, Charter, internet and dot-com companies, semiconductors)
sectors.real_estate: commercial real estate, REITs, property as an investment
sectors.commodities_gold: gold, silver, farmland, commodities as investments
sectors.transportation_other: trucking, logistics, autos and car dealerships (BYD, Berkshire Hathaway Automotive), trailer and equipment leasing (XTRA)
sectors.services_distribution_other: distribution and service businesses: McLane (grocery and foodservice distribution), Pilot Flying J (travel centers), TTI (electronic components), CORT (furniture rental), Business Wire, Pampered Chef, Kirby, Pinkerton's, Blue Chip Stamps (trading stamps)
sectors.steel_metals_mining: steel, metals, mining companies (Precision Steel, Handy & Harman, Kaiser Aluminum, POSCO)

themes.inflation: inflation, purchasing power, how inflation hurts investors or businesses
themes.interest_rates: interest rates, the Fed, monetary policy, rates and stock values
themes.bonds_fixed_income: bonds, Treasuries, junk bonds, fixed income as an investment. Preferred stock and convertibles go to preferred_convertible_investments instead.
themes.preferred_convertible_investments: preferred stocks and convertible securities as investments (Salomon, Gillette, USAir, Champion, First Empire, American Express Percs, Goldman Sachs, GE, Bank of America, Heinz, Occidental preferreds)
themes.arbitrage_workouts: merger arbitrage and workouts: buying into announced deals, liquidations and other corporate events for a spread. Berkshire buying a whole business is acquisitions_deals.
themes.market_valuation: the overall level of stock prices, bubbles, overvaluation, the market's prospects. If both this and market_timing_forecasts fit, use market_valuation when the passage judges the price level, market_timing_forecasts when it is about whether anyone can predict markets or the economy.
themes.market_timing_forecasts: forecasting, market timing, economic predictions, fear and greed (see market_valuation for the tie-break)
themes.cash_liquidity: cash holdings, liquidity, never depending on the kindness of strangers
themes.debt_leverage: borrowing, leverage, margin, debt at Berkshire or others; also Clayton's lending to home buyers
themes.derivatives: derivatives contracts, equity puts, credit default contracts, counterparty risk
themes.buybacks: share repurchases at Berkshire or other companies. A repurchase passage gets buybacks only, unless it also discusses dividends or the general retain-versus-distribute choice (then add dividends_capital_allocation).
themes.dividends_capital_allocation: dividends, retained earnings, capital allocation decisions (see buybacks for the tie-break)
themes.acquisitions_deals: buying businesses, acquisition criteria, deal terms, prices paid
themes.intrinsic_value_book_value: intrinsic value, book value, per-share measures, how to value Berkshire. A passage that only reports the year's book-value or per-share result is berkshire_performance; add this key only when the passage explains the measure. Intrinsic value as a general method for valuing any business is investing_principles.
themes.accounting_reporting: GAAP, accounting rules, look-through earnings, goodwill, reporting quality. Pension accounting goes to pensions_retirement_accounting.
themes.pensions_retirement_accounting: pension funds and their return assumptions, pension liabilities and accounting, retirement plans
themes.taxes: corporate and investor taxes, deferred taxes, tax policy
themes.float_underwriting: insurance float, underwriting profit or loss, combined ratio, reserves. Always comes with sector insurance; an insurer passage without float or underwriting economics gets sector insurance only.
themes.catastrophe_risk: super-cats, catastrophe exposure, risk management in insurance
themes.management_governance: managers, boards, CEOs, executive compensation, stock options, corporate governance
themes.succession_culture: succession planning, Berkshire's culture and structure
themes.shareholder_programs: Berkshire's shareholder programs and owner relations: shareholder-designated contributions, the owner's manual, the shareholder base and how Berkshire communicates with owners. Class B shares and splits are stock_issuance_splits.
themes.index_funds_fees: index funds, investment fees, active management, helpers
themes.currency_trade_deficit: the dollar, foreign exchange, trade deficits, foreign investment
themes.government_fiscal_policy: government deficits, national debt, fiscal policy, bailouts
themes.regulation_politics: regulation, regulators, political and legal environment
themes.investing_principles: general investing method: Ben Graham, Mr. Market, margin of safety, circle of competence, temperament, diversification versus concentration, long-term holding, intrinsic value as a method, critique of efficient-market theory and beta, owner earnings, 'wonderful business at a fair price' as a rule. Why one specific business has pricing power is moats_competitive_advantage; whether forecasts are useful is market_timing_forecasts.
themes.moats_competitive_advantage: economic franchises, moats, pricing power, wonderful businesses (see investing_principles for the tie-break)
themes.berkshire_performance: Berkshire's yearly results, performance vs the S&P 500, record over time (see intrinsic_value_book_value for the tie-break)
themes.stock_issuance_splits: issuing shares, class B shares, stock splits, mergers paid in stock
themes.climate_esg: climate change, renewable commitments, social responsibility
themes.american_economy_outlook: the American economy's long-term prospects, tailwind, optimism about America
